claude.country: Belgium (multicentre: Netherlands, USA, Brazil, China, Germany, Israel)
claude.sample_unit: participants with Parkinson's disease (85 local, 256 external)

links.outcome: External-cohort agreement (ICC %TF) before vs after fine-tuning on local annotated data
links.effect: Fine-tuning with 50 min of external data raised mean ICC(%TF) from 0.562 to 0.732 ± 0.138 (+30.2%) and ICC(#FOG) from 0.298 to 0.623 ± 0.214 (+108.9%); more data-efficient than training from scratch.
links.quote: At that point, fine-tuned ICC(%TF) reached 0.732 ± 0.138 (+30.2 %), and ICC(#FOG) reached 0.623 ± 0.214 (+108.9 %).

links.outcome: Performance drop of model on external cohorts versus local cohort
links.effect: ICC(%TF) fell from 0.886 locally to 0.562 ± 0.141 on external cohorts; ICC(#FOG) 0.298 ± 0.270; false positives per non-FOG trial rose to 1.690.
links.quote: When tested on the external cohorts (Table 3 ), agreement in terms of FOG severity dropped: mean ICC for %TF across external datasets reduced to 0.562 ± 0.141

links.outcome: Performance variation across sites and sensor configurations
links.effect: Performance varied by cohort; per-dataset ICC(%TF) pre-trained ranged from 0.417 to 0.824, with many false positives in cohorts with 1-2 IMUs and poor results in the Mobilise-D cohort.
links.quote: Similarly, Fig. 3 c, d, and f illustrate the model’s tendency to generate multiple FPs in datasets with only one or two IMUs, i.e., Federal, Twente, and Xuanwu

links.outcome: Dataset shift from task, annotation criteria, sensor setup, and patient spectrum differences
links.effect: Cohort differences (tasks, annotation criteria, IMU number, mild freezers) reduced pre-trained model performance; Mobilise-D mild freezers had shortest episodes (0.983 s) and smallest fine-tuning gains.
links.quote: Additionally, detecting FOG in the predominantly mild-freezer Mobilise-D cohort was particularly challenging, illustrating the risks of applying models trained on severe freezers to mildly affected populations.

links.outcome: Generalization of model trained on one cohort to new populations and contexts
links.effect: Agreement dropped from ICC(%TF) 0.886 locally to 0.562 externally; #FOG ICC fell to 0.298 (poor).
links.quote: This reduction reflects a lowered agreement in both %TF and #FOG, showing that differences between cohorts can reduce model performance.

links.outcome: Effect of simulated expert review (false-positive removal) on model agreement in Radboud cohort
links.effect: Simulated expert removal of FPs increased ICC(%TF) from 0.481 to 0.893 and ICC(#FOG) from 0.098 to 0.642 in the Radboud cohort.
links.quote: This correction markedly improved agreement with ground truth annotations, as shown in Table 3 , increasing ICC(%TF) from 0.481 to 0.893 and ICC(#FOG) from 0.098 to 0.642.

links.outcome: Annotation reliability and variability of reference standard across cohorts and raters
links.effect: Differing annotation criteria across cohorts; Xuanwu criteria not reported; for Mobilise-D a third rater vs ground truth ICC was 0.757 (%TF) and 0.543 (#FOG), showing intrinsic rater difficulty.
links.quote: These findings suggest that FOG detection in the Mobilise-D dataset is intrinsically challenging, even for experienced human raters.

unlisted_practices: Fine-tuning pretrained model with limited (~50 min) annotated local data versus training from scratch
Human-in-the-loop expert review and iterative fine-tuning workflow for AI annotation

openai.country: Belgium; Netherlands; United States; Brazil; Germany; Israel; China

links.outcome: external validation agreement
links.effect: Performance dropped from local ICC(%TF)=0.886 and ICC(#FOG)=0.573 to external ICC(%TF)=0.562 ± 0.141 and ICC(#FOG)=0.298 ± 0.270.
links.quote: Our results showed that while the DLA model achieved strong agreement on the local KU Leuven cohort for %TF (ICC = 0.886, CI = [0.79, 0.90]) and fair agreement for #FOG (ICC = 0.573, CI = [0.28, 0.71]), its performance dropped on the external datasets, averaging fair agreement for %TF (ICC = 0.562 ± 0.141, CI = [−0.01, 0.78]) and poor agreement for #FOG (ICC = 0.298 ± 0.270, CI = [−0.16, 0.49]).

links.outcome: architecture selection by ICC
links.quote: LTContext was selected for further experiments, as it achieved the highest ICC for both %TF and #FOG across all external datasets.

links.outcome: agreement after local fine-tuning
links.effect: Fine-tuning with 50 min improved ICC(%TF) to 0.732 ± 0.138 (+30.2%) and ICC(#FOG) to 0.623 ± 0.214 (+108.9%).
links.quote: Our analysis demonstrated that fine-tuning the model reached a plateau for both ICC(%TF) and ICC(#FOG) using 50 min of annotated data for training, with improved ICC(%TF) to 0.732 ± 0.138 (+30.2%) and ICC(#FOG) to 0.623 ± 0.214 (+108.9%).

links.outcome: expert false-positive removal
links.effect: Expert FP removal increased ICC(%TF) from 0.481 to 0.893 and ICC(#FOG) from 0.098 to 0.642.
links.quote: This correction markedly improved agreement with ground truth annotations, as shown in Table 3 , increasing ICC(%TF) from 0.481 to 0.893 and ICC(#FOG) from 0.098 to 0.642.

links.outcome: false positives from missing IMU channels
links.effect: Pre-trained #FPs/trial were 4.787 Federal, 1.052 Twente, and 2.462 Xuanwu in one/two-IMU datasets.
links.quote: Similarly, Fig. 3 c, d, and f illustrate the model’s tendency to generate multiple FPs in datasets with only one or two IMUs, i.e., Federal, Twente, and Xuanwu, potentially due to zero-filling of missing channels to match the 5-IMU input of the pre-trained model.

links.outcome: ground-truth annotation reliability
links.effect: In 29 Mobilise-D trials, third rater versus ground truth ICC was 0.757 for %TF and 0.543 for #FOG.
links.quote: The ICC between the fine-tuned model and the original ground truth was 0.540 for %TF and 0.756 for #FOG, whereas the ICC between the third rater and the ground truth was 0.757 and 0.543, respectively.

links.outcome: freezing of gait severity agreement across external cohorts
links.effect: mean ICC for %TF dropped from 0.886 locally to 0.562 ± 0.141 across external datasets, and ICC for #FOG dropped from 0.573 to 0.298 ± 0.270
links.quote: When tested on the external cohorts (Table 3 ), agreement in terms of FOG severity dropped: mean ICC for %TF across external datasets reduced to 0.562 ± 0.141 (mean ± standard deviation (SD) across six datasets; 95% CI [-0.01, 0.78]) and for #FOG to 0.298 ± 0.270 (mean ± SD across six datasets; 95 % CI [-0.16, 0.49]).

links.outcome: freezing of gait detection agreement after fine-tuning
links.effect: fine-tuned ICC for %TF reached 0.732 ± 0.138 (+30.2%) and ICC for #FOG reached 0.623 ± 0.214 (+108.9%) with 50 minutes of external cohort data
links.quote: At that point, fine-tuned ICC(%TF) reached 0.732 ± 0.138 (+30.2 %), and ICC(#FOG) reached 0.623 ± 0.214 (+108.9 %).

screen.practice: local fine-tuning and human-in-the-loop expert review
screen.reason: Evaluates multicentre validation and tests whether local fine-tuning with limited external data alongside expert review mitigates cohort heterogeneity for sensor-based freezing of gait assessment.
